One of my favorite games, The story line is amazing.

Graphics - Especially for a 2010 game, the graphics are amazing, you can get some really amazing scenery in this, Not quite on the level of Skyrim, But looking over the map is very nice to do :)
Gameplay - The gameplay is very easy to get used to, from stealth missions to full out combat, this game gives you some brilliant gunfights, robberies, boss missions and car chases. The police evasion is a very tedius, but over all more fun method, Unlike games like GTA where, you loose the police and you can then drive past them with a car thats smashed up, covered in blood with bullet holes in it and they won't beat an eye, this game requires you to get your car fixed up, new plates added, and a change of clothes to get the police to not suspect anything next time they see you.
Controls - The controls are very nicely done, as far as combat is concerned, the aiming, the slow motion, everything is brilliant. As for driving, They have gone for realism with it, Some people might like it, I wasn't really a fan of it, it takes a bit of time to get used to meaning I spent most of the beginning of the game crashing into things and getting shot up in no time, but with a bit of practice you become a good driver in no time, But then again, its realistic, its how cars where back then. 
Story - One of my favorite stories of all time, I can't really describe it, but you will have to play it to find out. Its a whole story of betrayal, emotion, sadness but at the same time, partying, trust, money. The story is a crazy mix of family life and gang life. The best way to describe it, is sort of on par with Breaking bad. A hardworking man taking up illegal tasks to help support his family.

[h1]This review is based on a purely vanilla playthrough.[/h1]

+ While the graphics are nothing special, they seem to have aged well
+ Top-shelf voice acting for the entire cast
+ Getting in trouble with the police is much more interactive than many other products of this genre, allowing you to pay fines, bribe officers, or attempt resistance on-site
+ Fist-fighting mechanics are cinematic, intuitive and entertaining
+ There is a speed-limiter key for toggling "safe driving mode;" a massive quality-of-life feature that every free-roam game should have
+ Game boasts very competent storytelling, with an even pace and solid character development
+ Has a great cliffhanger ending; seeing the story through to the end felt worth it
+ Every aspect of the aesthetics, from the clothes, to the vehicles and music, is period-appropriate and has a pervading feeling of authenticity
+ Vehicle handling feels realistic and smooth
+ Stock, reliabe cover system and shooting mechanics; nothing you haven't seen before, but the devs seemed to have settled with the 'less is more' approach, and it complemented the gameplay nicely
+ Engine optimization is excellent
+ While the explorable area is more of a medium size compared to competitors, there is still much to explore throughout the game world, and it feels appropriately sized for a small city
+ Active modding community, and the game itself is easy to alter
+ Some minimalist stealth mechanics that are well-implemented, though it isn't often revisited

- Many crashes; I've heard that this game has problems with AMD cards, though, so NVIDIA users may not have these issues
- Poor weapon selection (only about 7-8 usable firearms)
- No side missions, and little in the way of collectibles or extra content (though I cannot speak to the DLC); little replayability
- NPCs feel flat and generic, doing little to liven up the atmosphere of the city
- Lack of post-campaign free-roam (though a simple mod can fix this if you don't mind the small hassle)

If you're looking for a free-roaming game like Grand Theft Auto, fuhgeddaboutit. Mafia 2 has an open world, stores to shop at or rob, a police system, and many other things you'd expect from that sort of game, but like Mafia 1, the game is a lot more structured, and instead of having much in terms of side content it plays out like a traditional game campaign, with little time for free roaming. But the game's world is still well-designed, even if it's mostly pretty window dressing, and it makes the campaign feel more alive than it would if it was just a corridor shooter. It's not an amazing game, but it is a unique one. Mafia 2 is the kind of game where the police are actually police, and even though they'll probably never catch you they'll still try to ticket you for breaking the speed limit. It's the kind of game that isn't afraid to be a little tedious to give a sense of contrast between a "normal life" and the mafia life, like an early level that has you packing crates into the back of a truck to test your patience until you give up and leave. The developers do a good job at recreating the time period, and the cars, radio, and weapons all handle and sound pretty nice. The story and gunplay are both pretty well-done, and overall if you're a fan of mafia stories like The Godfather than Mafia 2 is worth a shot, as long as you don't go in expecting a true open world game.

[h1]Why Mafia II will always remain one of the most memorable games of all time!![/h1]

[b]ATTENTION TO DETAIL[/b]
The level of detail in Mafia II is just unbelievable. The first thing you will notice are the set pieces and let me just say they're breathtaking. 2K Czech have crafted a perfect 1950s world design. The world looks so alive, the buildings, the interiors, cars, the people passing down the streets - the developers took care of every single detail here. You'll see people minding their own work like reading newspapers, fixing cars, using the phone booth, workers on duty like cleaning or moving shipments. But that's not all. You can have a snack or a bottle of beer to replenish your health, it's more important than you realize because you don't regain a full 100% health bar without eating, I ended up forgetting about this quiet often. You can interact with objects in your apartment. The suits and jackets in-game aren't flat textures, all of them are richly detailed and even move while sprinting. All these details add an immersion to the game.

[b]STORY[/b]
Mafia II already excels in aesthetics but I feel the biggest selling point of Mafia II is if of course - its rich narrative driven plot. The story and characters are so well written, uh...without spoiling or giving away too much, I'll just say if Mafia II was made into a movie it would have been nominated for several awards. There's everything you would expect from a gangster story. The developers did not shy to overlook mature themes. There's blood and violence, real tension between the factions. Vito Scalletta is the protagonist of the main game and he is very likable and charming character - which is a good thing. Joe Barbaro is the secondary protagonist and he is just amazing, his personality is the opposite from Vito and it blends and works perfect! Story is divided into 15 chapters, each taking place on a different date. Every character you interact with feel naturals and real. Voice acting, lip-sync, accents used by the Mafia and supporting characters is fantastic. 

Players who've returned after playing the original game will be rewarded with a mission that at the later part of the game. You'll be surprised when you realize how the first game connects to 2002's Mafia. I'll advise to play Mafia 1 remake before jumping on this entry!!

[b]GAMEPLAY[/b]

1. DRIVING - You'll spend a lot of time driving. There are at least different 40 cars you can drive. Mafia II takes place in the span of around 8 years so don't get disappointed if you see crappy cars early on as new and better cars are kept for the later parts. There are sport cars and they drive like a plane!! Nearly every vehicle can be modified, repainted. Cars you steal can be legalized by changing the number plates. You can also improve and upgrade the horsepower, you can repair your cars you will do that and no, the cars you damage do not get auto-repaired once you put them in your garage which look so realistic. If you crash your car, you need to get out repair it manually. Cars also get as much detail as other things in the game. 

2. GUNPLAY - Its great, you'll be amazed how intense it gets you're in a fight. Enemy A.I is intelligent and will shoot you at sight. It's very challenging on highest difficulty. You can try shooting at stuff and watch everything just break apart in in-door fights. Every object is a separate object and not a 2D texture. You can shoot and damage shelves, paintings, little containers and walls. When you kill a shop owner or a civilian, you are wanted by the cops which is not uncommon but you'll be surprised that the police will investigate the crime scene and will seal the shop/crime area when you try to got back which is just amazing. Which modern AAA game really does that? Turn on Nvidia Physx to max and you'll love watches things such as stones, glass, metal crumble and break apart into tiny pieces.

[b]GRAPHICS, SOUND & MUSIC[/b] - You're looking at the most detailed game of 2010 (Just cause 2 comes second). Great choice of licensed music from the 50s. I'm a little worried as the licences might soon expire. Hurry up!!

[h1]Things that you might dislike[/h1]
-One of my biggest complaints about the open world design is that it's LINEAR. It was really sad to see there was nothing to do once the story missions were complete. No side missions and activities.
-Manual saving and loading would have been much better instead of checkpoint save system. 
-Cops will try to fine you a ticket if you dash other cars or try race over 40 kmph. I like the realism however it becomes a pain when you just want to enjoy the game. 
-collectables are missable and specific to chapter. 

[h1]Should you buy Mafia 2[/h1]
YESSS.....One of the best Stories told in a video game. Even with its few missteps, Mafia II won't disappoint you. Mafia 2 (Classic is included as a part of Definitive Edition).

This game looks great at almost 10 years old playing it in 2019. The performance is great too with only one issue with the Physx graphics option. Which I think can be fixed by installing the older driver version but I just kept it turned off. It supports 4K resolutions and it looks great in 4K while the sound is also pretty awesome with some great music from the period. 

The game world is very immersive with a lot of attention to detail and some fun collectables. The story is pretty good even if it does feel rushed in places and they could have spent more time developing some elements. It feels like a collection of elements from many different gangster movies which is fun to see. It’s a genre style story too which doesn’t take itself too seriously with some over the top violence.

The weapons are fun to use, they sound great even if the animations are a little bit clunky. Actually the animations in general are a little bit rough around the edges and are maybe one of the few things that actually do show this games` age. Walking up stairs for example is the same as walking on a flat surface which looks hilarious but can break immersion.  

The missions are immersive and fun to play through with one particular moment half way through that is really cool and unexpected. The story does start to get a bit repetitive but there are some genuinely interesting cutscenes and characters along the way. The music is genuinely awesome with classic tunes from the period that made me want to listen to more from the individual artists. The story does end very abruptly though and it actually feels like they didn’t expect people to play past a certain point because they just wrap it all up so awkwardly in the last few missions.

Overall Mafia 2 is a very well made and fun to play game which does some specific things very well. Even if it is lacking in depth and content compared to other open world games.

Before trying to play this game on a modern PC it's recommended to install the 4 GB patch, which can be found in the Guides section of the Community tab for this game. If you don't do that, your game will probably freeze and/or crash after a few minutes of gameplay.

The main attraction of this game is the story, and I think an average player will find it neat and will enjoy Vito and Joe's "bromance". It's a typical story about criminals who try to achieve the American dream by any means and face the consequences of their actions. You end up cheering for the main characters, despite the fact they're not very good people. The game's tight pace and lack of time-wasting filler content is also a nice change from your average open-world game.

For those who want to spend more time with the game there are 2 types of collectibles: Wanted posters and Playboy magazines, the latter is probably some of the best collectibles in the history of videogames (for obvious reasons), but they do come with an annoyance – many of them can only be collected during specific chapters of the story, which means you'll have to replay the chapters in which you've missed them.

Then there are the DLCs. I suggest skipping straight to Joe's Adventures DLC, since it's the only one that deserves attention and feels like a worthy addition to the main game. Its missions have good variety and take place in new locations. It's perfect for scratching that itch for more content that you might still have after finishing the base game.

Jimmy's Betrayal DLC: it features no cutscenes except for the beginning and the end of the DLC, all missions are dull and uninspired, they ask you to either shoot or melee fight someone, or deliver a vehicle. As a "cherry" on top, the 2 final missions of this DLC recycle the locations that were already used for shootouts in the main game, making the whole thing feel like an afterthought, thrown together last minute for the release of the game. I only recommend it if Joe's Adventures wasn't enough for you and you don't mind consuming something a bit "sloppy".

Jimmy's Vendetta DLC: same level of sloppiness as the Jimmy's Betrayal DLC, but at least the final mission takes place in a new location.

Mafia 2 probably won't blow your socks off if you're new to it, but it can still be enjoyed for what it is – a simple drivey-shootey gangster game with a decent story.

Probably the best game in the series. At least for me, it definitely is.

Compared to the first game, which sometimes feels like a rushed fanfic of The Godfather, where you meet the mafia boss in the first minutes and become his right-hand man almost immediately, Mafia II takes a much more grounded approach.

There’s no huge, over-the-top chain of events. Instead, the story feels slower, more believable, and closer to reality.

[h3]The characters here are dirt.[/h3]

They are real scumbags, people you wouldn’t want anything to do with in real life. But the game forces you into their world. And over time, it feels like Vito is slowly becoming just like them.

[h3]Atmosphere & Aging[/h3]

Despite its age, the game still holds up very well.

Thanks to a recommendation from a close friend, I started this game with mild expectations. I did not think that by the end of the game, it would become my favorite game of all-time. These are a few reasons why.

1. The shooting and aiming in this game is amazing. The gunfights are super fun to play (Although some get tiring when you've replayed it 5 or six times). 
2. The characters' dynamics, interactions, and developments are spot on. Never have I seen a game where the characters work so well with each other. No character is dull, and no character is too pointless to be forgotten.
3. The story itself is the best story I have ever seen in a video game. No chapter gets annoying, and no chapter is dull. Each one adds something new and exciting, making this game fun to play even after the tenth time.
4. The final mission is one of the best final missions I have ever played. It adds to the ambience of the whole story, and you feel like a badass the entire time. It was so much fun to play, and I will play it many times afterwards.
5. The ending. I will not spoil the ending, but everything in the game leading up to this ending is all worth it. I have never shaken at a game's ending before, and this one was the first. I had to take a 5 minute breather just to accept and intake the ending. It was one of the best endings, if not THE best, ending of a video game.

These are a few of the reasons why I love this game.

Most people love the first game. It was original, brutally mature, and insanely addictive.

In this game, you start as a soldier in WW2 where you see some intense "Brothers in Arms" action.

Next, the game brings you back to the States in February, 1945 - and I won't spoil the storyline any further.

The game doesn't throw you into driving right away. you actually get to enjoy the view of the city.

The cut scenes are interesting to watch to say the least. I like GTA games, but I don't remember being able to sit through a single cut scene, it just never stuck with me. However, in Mafia 2 as well as Red Dead Redemption, you DO want to watch the cut scenes. Read Dead for instance, was filled with some good, albeit heavy well-thought out secular life philosophy. That isn't exactly the case in this game, this IS a gangster game after all. However, it IS impressive how they managed to keep the story strong without resorting to the well-known cliches that are associated with Italian gangsters, plus there is some good vulgarity, nudity, adult magazines and great original one-liners.

The attention to detail is simply outstanding. I wouldn't be surprised if the developers hadn't taken their time to create every shelf, every book and every street corner for that matter, with the utmost care to detail. The NPC models are numerous and if you dont scrutinize the NPCs too much, you just wont often find same NPCs, just let the game flow over you. The interior designs are amazing too look at and the icy roads are a b1tch to drive on.

Having played the demo, and getting my first glimpse at the map, I was disappointed. It is small in comparison to Just Cause 2 and Red Dead, which is still a bit of a turn off for me. HOWEVER, the major point is how they managed to utilize the city to its fullest potential. Meaning, the miscellaneous stores and buildings often have an interior with and without people that you can see, which only adds to the sheer depth of the city. You actually get a feel that you are standing next to an apartment building filled with people. In GTA series, buildings were but lifeless texture blocks. Also, there are plenty of missions that take place inside buildings. One of them, involving a safe, will put a long smile on your face as you listen to the conversation between the two security guards. The shootouts are okay, the usual shoot -take cover type of action. The funny thing is that whilst completing the shooting missions, I found myself wasting time by observing the details of furniture and other objects which are greatly polished.

Its also fun to see the well-familiar WW2 American propaganda posters. Remember, the walls have ears... There are plenty of artifacts in the game indicating your 1940's era. Babe Ruth's posters, movie posters and what not.

Some random conversations in the game are outright genius. "Extra! extra! I am freezing my ball$ out here..." or "Spending nights with Rosy Palm and her five sisters" are just a few of them.

The radio broadcast gives an incredible insight into how people talked and thought. The then-live broadcast of WW2 events and battles is interesting enough for you to stand and listen, getting more and more immersed in the game.

I also wouldn't mean hearing some original Italian Language with English subtitles. That is how I played Assassin's Creed II actually.
The lock pick system is reminiscent of the Watchmen game, but it is MUCH easier to handle

Another cool thing is that you can pimp your ride, AND you can customize your plates. Go vulgarity!

Also, for those of you still yearning for the good old days of the first game, tune in Empire Radio whilst driving and feel yourself get a decade younger for a moment.

The Brooklyn Bridge replica is impeccable. I ride the Brooklyn Bridge on my bike quite a few times every summer, and let me tell you, the game nailed it the bridge where GTA 4 failed. Enough said. Also, there is a nice replica of the Brooklyn-Bridge Expressway as you take the right exit off of the Brooklyn Bridge - on the Brooklyn Side.
The docs are also in the right place.

The fist fighting is reminiscent of the Bourne Supremacy game, plus there are some cool easy-to-pull of combo moves

The cut scenes actually retain the car damage that you may have sustained completing a mission

The BAD:

The lip sync is not exactly top notch, in fact its bad.
You can tell they just had the characters flapping their pie holes whilst adding the relative dialogue. I guess only Bioware can pull a well-made lip sync, among other companies.

I also think that the main character could use a bit more charisma and inner thoughts just like Tommy in the first game.

Another thing is that after a couple of hours of playing, you find that there isn't really much to do in the city besides enjoying the scenery, driving and going to bars. But, I guess that's why the developers tried to push the game into linear play in an open-world map.

But it's all good. The city itself is a part of the story and while you don't get to visit every corner in the city during the story line it is sitll nice to know that you can explore this very polished world.  It is sad that the game's engine hasn't been used since in many other game, it really has a lot of potential.

All I can say emotionally is "WOW".

Mafia II is a masterpiece that never gets old. I’ve completed it countless times, earned all the achievements, and it’s still one of my all-time favorites. The game’s world is so immersive, and the narrative so compelling, that even after multiple playthroughs, I still enjoy it as much as the first time. Highly recommend it to anyone who loves deep stories and great gameplay.

Mafia 2's story is great, most characters are well written and the missions are good enough. Difficulty is not that harsh like it was in the previous game, although you can make it tough with the highest difficulty and also with realistic driving and there are still a few missions which can give a bit of a headache. The atmosphere is still very good and feels authentic, thanks to the soundtrack as well. Graphics look great, even though the game is more than 10 years old. Controls are fine, you need to get used to the driving and some of the key bindings but it's alright.

However, this game has its own problem on modern systems and most times it can crash a lot or the graphics can glitch. To fix this, you need to use the 4GB patch from [url=https://ntcore.com/4gb-patch/]here[/url], and patch the [b]mafia2.exe[/b] at .../steamapps/common/Mafia 2/pc. After that, all of those issues should get fixed (it got for me) and now Mafia 2 uses 4 GB virtual memory instead of 2 GB.

But this issue is not really the game's fault, but there are a few things which could have been better in Mafia 2, and one of them is the AI. Overall, the friendly AIs in gun fights are not doing too much or anything, meanwhile the enemies (especially in later chapters) will aimbotting and shoot you on sight, depending what weapon they have they can push you without trying to protect themselves. The police AI is also questionable, because sometimes they don't react to you if you are speeding right in front of them, but sometimes they notice you when you are speeding behind them. Or they can lose you in places where you are open to find or easy to find you but sometimes they can magically see you through walls and also they are ruthless in car chases... they are really inconsistent in general.
Then, there were parts in the story which felt overdone, too long and one of them for example [spoiler] is the prison parts. I get it that the story needs to build up Leo and Vito's connection, but this part was just too long without much interesting part for me. [/spoiler]
There is the checkpoint system, which works fair and square but sometimes checkpoints are too far from each other on certain missions which makes them difficult to complete if you die a lot in them, although this part is more to the challenging aspect rather than a problem for me.

Mafia 2 has DLCs as well, which are additional cars and clothing. There are even 3 DLC stories to follow which are standalone from the story mode, which sounds exciting on paper.

[b]Betrayal of Jimmy[/b]
This is basically an open world mode for Mafia 2 with a bunch of missions and to give an "arcade experience for the player", playing with a guy who looks like a budget Mr. Clean, but his name is Jimmy. Jimmy is a gun for hire, and in this DLC he will work for Sal Gravina on the Italian Mafia side and for Tam Brodie who is leading his Irish Brodie gang. Jimmy's job is to help them to eliminate their competition in a total of 24 missions.
This DLC has nothing to do with the main story (although some of it's missions are played on key locations from the main story), doesn't contain any character from there neither, which is not big of a deal, but to be fair this one has no real story or characters (Jimmy is deep as a character like a cardboard) to follow and the missions are also gets repetitive and some of them are really difficult, and on top of that the missions has a time limit to complete, and if you miss that you have to restart the whole mission, and some of them are takes a decent time to start it anyway. Not even mentioning that some mission's mechanics are not really working properly, for example missions which include cars with explosives in it and you are supposed to drive them carefully, they are never exploding for any contact... at least they never did in my playtime. Difficulty will come from either you having barely enough time to finish the objectives, or you have to deal with a bunch of enemies and also have to deal with the police continuously. And what is the craziest thing to me is that this DLC is almost as long as the main story mode, this takes 4-5 hours to playthrough, and the story mode is around 5-6 hours which is really crazy to think about.
In the end, the DLC tries to connect the dots and gives the illusion for an epilogue on this non existent story, where [spoiler]Jimmy gets set up when he goes for his reward when the police catches him with drug in his reward car, he will be sent to prison but promises to himself to take his revenge on those who set him up, on his former employers.[/spoiler]
And to explain it further, throughout the whole DLC the player collects points from missions and from the free play part in order to get a good placement in the leaderboards, and that's basically the "arcade experience".
Honestly the whole thing is just a big miss, and has the most annoying game elements of Mafia 2. Do not play it.

[b]Jimmy's Vendetta[/b]
It continues what the last DLC started story wise (even though that was not much to begin with), and in this one Jimmy wants to take his revenge on those who wronged him in the past in 28 missions now.
This DLC is basically the same as the previous one, except that Jimmy's Vendetta is more forgiving with the difficulty. It still has some quite difficult missions, but most of them are manageable and the time limits are not too bad either.
The final mission sets on a new place on the map, so that's a bit of a change and something nice to see, although enemies can occasionally wallbang you here.
In the end of the DLC [spoiler]Jimmy deals with the gang leader and head of the Italian family, however Jimmy goes for the Judge as well, who allegedly managed both groups and sent Jimmy to prison. Jimmy kills the Judge as well and that ends the Vendetta.[/spoiler]
This one is a little bit bearable and takes 4 hours to playthrough, but there is no reason to play this one at all.

[b]Joe's Adventure[/b]
This DLC focuses on Joe and fills the plot holes in the main story starting from Chapter 5, which sounds good for those who are interested more about the game's story. It basically shows how Joe meets with Eddie Scarpa and how he makes connections with his family.
The introductory mission is really good and fun, fits perfectly with the Mafia 2 missions from the story mode. It gives high hopes for the player after the two DLC...
but other than that, I think this is by far the worst DLC to play. The gameplay and even most missions are the same as in the other DLCs, except that there are occasionally proper story missions, but they are not that well made as the first one was. The reason I really don't like this one is the difficulty, which ramps up massively here. More active and annoying police, really picky mission states, difficult timed missions, aimbotting enemies and missions where you need to know ahead what will happen, otherwise you are done.
Getting through the 25 missions that this DLC contains is painful, it took me 5 hours in total.

So all in all, the base Mafia 2 game is fun and alright it has some points which could be annoying or could have been done better, but all in all fine. Any other additional content except the clothing and the cars are horrible tho, so only play the base game which I recommend. 30€ with the Definitive Edition sounds a bit expensive, I would go with 20€ max for the two games.

Important notes before I start the review: If you’re running this game on a low-end PC, then go to the video options menu and set the video mode to 1280x720. You should also make sure that ambient occlusion, antialiasing, and “APEX PhysX” are off and that shadow quality and geometry detail are set to “Low”. Anisotropic filtering can be set to x16, but you can set it lower if you want. Vertical synchronisation and fullscreen can also stay on with little issue. I should also mention that buying this game (by buying the Definitive Edition), gives you all the DLCs, including some story ones like “Joe’s Adventures” and “The Betrayal of Jimmy”. Anyway, let’s begin! 

Mafia 2 is a sequel to the 2002 open world third-person shooter game, Mafia. This time, instead of playing in the city of Lost Heaven (based on Chicago) as a cab driver during the Prohibition Era, you’re playing in Empire Bay (based on New York) as a street thug called Vito Scaletta, who is arrested for a petty crime and given the choice to either go to jail or fight in WW2 for the Americans, specifically in Mussolini’s Italy. A couple years later, Vito is given a one month leave due to sustaining an injury in battle, but his childhood friend, Joe Barbaro, arranges a set of forged discharge papers so Vito doesn’t have to return to fighting in the war. From there, Vito finds out about his family’s debt and is determined to repay it. This is ultimately what brings him into the life of organised crime, changing his life forever. If you think this sounds interesting, then, by all means, keep reading. 

One aspect of Mafia 2 that I really like is the atmosphere. Overall, the 1940’s-50’s setting is very well done: the cars, music, architecture, etc. from that period are all present. There’s also a really interesting tonal choice that’s shown through the weather. After the WW2 mission in Sicily, the city of Empire Bay is gloomy and blanketed in snow. Days are cloudy and grey, and there isn’t much in terms of colour. However, after the war is over, the weather becomes much more pleasant, with lots of blue skies and sunny days. This part of the game also takes place in the 50’s, so the overall vibe of the place almost completely changes: new cars that are largely far more colourful than the ones prior, and new music, such as rock and roll, that is generally much more energetic and joyful than what you used to hear. The clothing that people wear is also radically different, with things like vibrant dresses and leather jackets becoming more commonplace. These changes in weather and overall style really reinforce the feeling that times have improved since the war. You also hear radio hosts humorously talk about many groundbreaking inventions, such as the takeaway meal, the TV remote, and the credit card, which further accentuates the feeling of progress and optimism in a new and more peaceful era. 

Another part of Mafia 2 that deserves praise is the plot. I genuinely loved watching Vito’s story unfold, seeing all the trouble he would get into and the things he’s required to do as a mafioso. I also liked meeting side characters like Joe, Eddie, Henry, etc., hearing their chemistry with Vito and each other, and seeing what happened to them as the story progressed. The story of a Sicilian immigrant child arriving in America and later entering the world of organised crime isn’t original, but that doesn’t matter. It’s clear that this game, like the first, is a love letter to Mafia movies by the likes of Scorsese and Ford Coppola, and that’s honestly wonderful. 

The gameplay is fine; it’s nothing groundbreaking, but it was enjoyable enough for me to keep playing the game and it felt more refined than in Mafia 1. Most of the combat sections are pretty standard for a third-person shooter: hide behind cover, shoot at enemies while hiding behind cover, etc. The shooting feels decent, with quite a large selection of weapons consisting of rifles and handguns for long range, submachineguns for medium range, and a shotgun for close range. The sounds of all the guns are distinct and satisfying to listen to, and peppering enemies with bullets and watching them slump to the ground was nice. Other than the guns, there are grenades and Molotov cocktails; using these was also quite fun, especially when enemies were bunched up together. There’s also melee combat, but it’s quite lacklustre, in my opinion. The driving feels great, and it actually incentivised me to steal some cars to add to my collection, as well as customise some that I grew particularly fond of. Much of the game you’ll spend driving around Empire Bay, either going to the next mission, escaping from cops, or buying ammo, clothes, food, etc. So, using cars is very important. 

Here’s where I want to talk about the negatives. My first gripe is that the open world could’ve been better. The city of Empire Bay is very much a set piece, and there isn’t much to do, not even side missions (the first Mafia game has side missions, yet this game doesn’t? Quite a shame). The game even has an NPC, Derek, who says he can give Vito jobs to do in his spare time, but nope, he never gives you any sort of small side job even once. To make up for this lack of side content, there are the aforementioned story DLCs included with the Steam version of Mafia 2. “Joe’s Adventures” was decent, with a nice variety of missions (although some were awful, such as “Bomb Under the Seat”). However, I couldn’t be bothered to finish “The Betrayal of Jimmy” or even start “Jimmy’s Vendetta”. From what little I played of “The Betrayal of Jimmy”, it was frustrating and poorly designed; the first mission wasn’t even registering my progress properly. “Jimmy’s Vendetta” is apparently full of repetitive arcade-like missions, so I decided not to touch it. As I mentioned before, the melee combat is quite lacklustre, with only the option of using your fists (Mafia 1 at least lets you use baseball bats). The melee fights themselves feel quite arcade-like, with you being locked onto whatever enemy you’re fighting and being prompted to do combos when you’ve done enough damage. This isn’t terrible, but it could’ve been much better, especially with actual melee weapon options. Another thing that I feel is a downgrade from the first game is the lack of the ability to ride a train or tram. It would’ve been really pleasant to just hop on a train and travel around the city, but sadly, that’s not an option. 

So, overall, Mafia 2 is an enjoyable experience and a worthy sequel to the first game. It’s quite flawed and a downgrade from the first game in quite a few aspects, but it’s still an improvement from it and worth playing through at least once. 

Final verdict: 7/10 “Ya shoot like my sister!”

Anyway, if you're looking for over-the-top fun and gameplay like in GTA or Saints Row, you won't get it here. This game's main focus is the story and the characters. You'll more often than not feel like you're playing a movie and waiting for another cutscene. Mafia 2 takes place during and after the 2nd world war and follows the story of Vito Scalleta and his best friend Joe Barbaro as they get involved with the Mafia. Without spoiling too much, the game takes some inspiration from the classic mafia movies, like The Godfather and The Goodfellas. I must also admit that I shed some tears on more than one occasion throughout the game. If you played the first Mafia, you'll also find a nod to the main character in one chapter, which recreates a certain event that happened in the first one.

Most of the Mafia II takes place in the fictional city of Empire Bay, which I think is based on New York and is fully explorable by the player. You are able to go pretty much anywhere with your vast collection of classic cars. The gunplay consists of using the cover-system and a variety of authentic weapons from that era, like MP40s, Thompsons and many more. The melee combat, while not on par with Sleeping Dogs or Batman games, is pretty good and challenging.

While the game is athmospheric and recreates the 40s and 50s very well, I must say that I'm dissapointed with the inconsistencies regarding the texture quality, most of it is good, but some things look considerably worse and can sometimes break the immersion. The game also suffers from some pretty noticable object pop-in. But, this game is one of the few, that does the depth of field right, I usually don't like DOF, but in this game it was very pretty. Also, the first part of the game takes place during the winter and the second part is during the summer, so It freshens up the game a bit.

If you're planing on buying it, you can safely purchase the base game without the DLC, which is more or less the cosmetic stuff. There are 2 'expansions', one of them has no story whatsoever and is very arcady (Jimmy's Vendetta) and the other one (Joe's Adventures) only has 1 mission which ties in to the main story.

In conclusion, if you like story rich games, like The Last of Us, Grand Theft Auto IV, Wolfenstein The New Order and so on, 
or if you like classic movies about the Mafia and awesome Italian accents, then by all means, get this game. You will not be disapointed. But if you're the type that skips all the cutscenes and doesn't care about the plot, then this game is not for you.

This game is good. I have seen some reviews calling it a masterpiece. I wouldn't go that far. It is a good game with a decent story, but it won't be a game I will play and play again. The game is set in the 1940's and 1950's eras and is based around the story of the rise of Vito from his days in the army to becoming a "made man". The world is relatively small compared with many open world games we see today but large enough to have some fun.

It is an enjoyable game, largely in part due to the great story and characters it has to offer but it does have it's problems.

First of all, Joe. He is one of Vito's friends in the game. His voice is the splitting image of Peter Griffin from Family Guy but in gangster mode. I can't take him seriously. There are rare, but random frame rate drops near to where some main interaction points will be, such as a building you may about to be entering. This happened only occasionally but enough to notice it.

There are various bugs in the game. I actually had the "Go back to Falcon" mission bug. This is a bug that appears after Chapter 7 and the mission icon on your mini map keeps reappearing on all future chapters making navigating using the mini map very difficult. You have to constantly manually select a way point to make it clear which mission you are supposed to be heading to. There was also a bug where Joe couldn't open a door during a mission which meant you could not exit the area. I had to spend 5 minutes trying to push him out the way so the door would open.

The AI on the map is sometimes slow to catch up with you. The police AI is useless. You can actually stay put inside a car in some cases and they will not move in on you and keep missing you with shots, on hardest difficulty! The AI across the worlds characters in general is pretty basic, even for 2011 games. It is very dumb! The XBOX One controller I used for the game was also limited in what you can do and the controls didn’t feel right.

When Vito walks, and even more so when he runs, it feels really slow and clunky. Not butter smooth like it should be. The camera angles are also quite odd I think. The choice of cars are limited in both eras and there are over 2 hours worth of cut scenes in a relatively short story. The wanted posters are meaningless within the game and I felt were not worth the hassle of collecting them all if you are not going for 100%. The city and world itself could do with some more colour and more variety. It felt rather dull.

Overall I really enjoyed the game, the story is brilliant, but this is definitely dated already and for a game to have a few minor issues this long after release and with my experience of Mafia 3 recently, I will not be buying any more Mafia games. You can't ruin a potentially good story and franchise with shoddy work. I don't support that kind of shit. This game is the best out of the two I have played and worth buying.

Too bad on my new pc it just bugs when the police wants to arrest you so sadly no replay :(

[b]What's Hot:[/b]
- Good plot
- Great story telling
- Beautiful environment and good graphics for its time
- Memorable characters
- Includes classic cars where each of them are handled differently
- Gunplay is decent for its time
- Use of old songs makes the game really come to life
- Collectibles are playboy magazines ( ͡ʘ ͜ʖ ͡ʘ) (Gotta collect'em all!)

[b]What's Not:[/b]
- You'll spend a lot of time driving around the city but, driving isn't enjoyable in this game, at least for me it isn't.
- Cops will try to fine you for speeding over 40kmph which is very annoying. Specially when you're in a hurry to complete a timed mission.
- I'm using a 144hz display which results in a bug where everything goes slowmo from the moment you are chased by police. The only fix is setting the refresh rate to 60hz from control panel as there are no in-game refresh rate settings to do so.
- Linear open-world design made me really sad as there was nothing to do once the story missions were complete. No side missions, no side activities, nothing.
- Checkpoint system of this game is just the worst. And there are no manual saving option either.

In my top 10 games for sure. The gameplay for nowadays standards isn't too bad but the story is unmatched. There have been only a few games in history for me that wrapped me around it's finger. The rise of Vito's story is beautiful yet tragic. If you have never played this, I highly recommend to do so.
